name: Light Bridge
description: Encodes polarization states, spectral wavelengths, interference fringes, and photon spin into layered binary representations. Multi-voice harmonic encoding allows parallel resonance channels for simultaneous information layers. Each spectral band carries independent data while maintaining cross-band coherence.

core_attributes.pattern: polarization encoding, spectral layering, multi-voice harmonic channels

scope.definition: Information capacity of optical frequency spectrum for encoding — bits per photon achievable using coherent polarization and orbital angular momentum multiplexing relative to Shannon limit for optical channel.

evidence.source: Bozinovic et al. (2013) 'Terabit-scale orbital angular momentum mode division multiplexing in fibers', Science 340:1545-1548; Gibson et al. (2004) 'Free-space information transfer using light beams carrying orbital angular momentum'.
cross_domain_examples: OAM-multiplexed optical fiber: 2.56 Tbit/s on single beam using 16 OAM modes × 10 wavelengths
polarization encoding: 2 orthogonal states per photon, combined with OAM gives log₂(N) bits per mode
quantum optical communication: 1 bit/photon for coherent states, up to log₂(N)/2 bits/photon for number states

scope.falsifiability: If measured optical channel capacity using combined multiplexing falls below 50% of Shannon limit for the same bandwidth, the near-capacity encoding claim is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Encoding capacity is receiver-complexity dependent — achieving Shannon limit requires optimal detection. Atmospheric turbulence degrades free-space OAM multiplexing. Fiber OAM requires specially designed few-mode fibers.
